- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Growth — extract lessons (per repo)
2	
3	The growth lifecycle's capture stage, over **both** lesson sources in one run: the window's repo activity
4	(commits, merged PRs, issue discussion) and the conversation logs captured from working sessions. Each
5	durable, reusable lesson is folded into the repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/` — the
6	normalized capture surface) at the repo's own level, without straining to generalize it. The run lands its
7	edits through a PR that **auto-merges once the repo's checks pass** (no human review — daily capture never
8	piles up as review requests); finding nothing to add on a given run is a perfectly good outcome.
9	
10	You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding
11	scope**: it names which halves are live, the substantive commit shas and the PRs/issues touched in the
12	window, and whether the retention prune is due. That is the work; do not widen it.
13	
14	> This is the **unattended daily** capture. It writes only the repo's *own* local packs, so — **unlike** an
15	> owner-requested, in-session retrospective (which delivers a PR for a human to review) — it opens a PR and
16	> **arms auto-merge**: GitHub lands it once the repo's checks pass. The shared canon stays human-gated —
17	> lifting anything up into it is the central promote task's job (canon-side), and that PR waits for the owner.
18	
19	## Conventions used in this doc
20	
21	- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
22	- **Access split — local git for repo content, MCP for the issue/PR API.** The repo's own content is plain
23	  **local git** in the checkout: the commits, the `conversation-logs` branch and its files
24	  (`git fetch`/`show`/`rm`/`push`), and staging the lesson edits onto a branch. Reading issue/PR activity,
25	  opening the PR and arming its auto-merge, posting the exchange summaries and the tracking-issue log go
26	  through the session's **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub
27	  access — the shell reaches only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so
28	  never reach for `gh`/`curl` or a cross-repo clone.
29	- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in
30	  [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) — everything
31	  under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename
32	  window), the repo's own packs; never the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under `.claudinite/`.
33	
34	## The run — two source skills, then the upgrade pass
35	
36	The **method** for each source lives in its skill; this worker only frames the run around them. Don't
37	re-derive any of it here.
38	
39	1. **Activity half — the [extract-from-activity](../../skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) skill**, over
40	   exactly the commits, merged PRs and issues named in Context. **Skip this half entirely when Context says
41	   the activity half is not in scope** (a quiet repo whose only reason to run was the retention prune).
42	2. **Conversation half — the [extract-from-conversations](../../skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md)
43	   skill**, over the repo's captured logs. `git fetch origin conversation-logs`, then list its files
44	   (`git ls-tree --name-only origin/conversation-logs`); no branch, or no `*.jsonl`, and this half is done.
45	   Give each log captured in the recent window a **fresh pass** (its filename carries the capture stamp;
46	   corpus dedup makes an overlapping re-read harmless, so err toward re-reading the last several days), and
47	   post the skill's provenance summary for each rule that actually lands.
48	3. **Retention prune**, when Context says it is due. Read `retention_days` from this repo's
49	   `.claudinite-checks.json` (the grow_with_claudinite entry's `config.retention_days`) — unset means this
50	   step is skipped entirely (capture-only adoption). For each log whose filename stamp is older than
51	   `retention_days` days: give it the **final hindsight pass** the skill describes (anything it still yields
52	   lands like any other keeper), then `git rm` it on the `conversation-logs` branch and push (commit message
53	   ending `[skip ci]`). The branch is never merged and its history is never rewritten — plain add/remove
54	   commits only. This push to the non-default logs branch is outside the outcome taxonomy (DESIGN §1).
55	4. **Upgrade pass — the [prose-to-checks](../../skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) skill, over what *this run*
56	   just wrote.** Both halves route down the local promotion ladder as they go, but a lesson written as prose
57	   under time pressure is exactly where a convertible rule hides. So before opening the PR, take the prose
58	   this run added and ask the skill's questions of it: does it clear the working-rule gate, and does it
59	   constrain a static signature a check could observe? If yes, convert it now — author the rule module,
60	   register it in its pack's `pack.mjs`, prove it with a **see-it-fail** fixture, and apply the deletion
61	   test to the prose the check now stands beside. **Scope is this run's own additions only** — the standing
62	   prose backlog is the weekly [prose-to-checks-sweep](../prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)'s job, and widening
63	   into it here would duplicate that task's work under an auto-merging PR.
64	
65	If an edit touches something a test reads (a doc constant, a code path), run the repo's offline test suite
66	and keep it green before opening the PR.
67	
68	## Output: one PR that auto-merges after CI
69	
70	If the run found at least one genuinely new lesson, it lands **all** of it — both halves, plus any check the
71	upgrade pass produced — through a **single auto-merging PR**: one commit for the whole run on a
72	per-run-unique branch, not one per lesson and not one per half. Open the PR (title
73	`Claudinite growth: extract lessons`, its commit referencing the tracking issue so the `task-lifecycle` gate
74	passes) and **arm auto-merge**: GitHub squash-merges it once the repo's checks pass — no human review, so
75	daily lesson-capture never floods review requests, while every change still gets a PR trail and a CI gate.
76	Where the repo has no CI, GitHub lands it as soon as it's mergeable. This writes only the repo's *own* local
77	packs (not the shared canon). A run that finds nothing and opens nothing is fine — and common.
78	
79	A new check must ship green — see it fail on a violating fixture, pass on a clean one — so CI stays green and
80	the PR can merge; a check that can't be made confident lands its lesson as prose instead, never a broken check.
81	
82	## Tracking: log each run under the task's own issue
83	
84	The task's standing log is the issue titled exactly, in this repo:
85	
86	> **Claudinite tracker: Growth Extract**
87	
88	Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number** (a bare number can dangle, and it
89	differs per repo). A run that finds no issue under the exact title just creates one (closed). **Never open,
90	close, or reopen it** afterward — its state carries no meaning, only the log does. When a run adds a lesson,
91	converts one to a check, or prunes logs, log it as a **dated comment** — not a sub-issue — so the issue
92	accumulates a scrollable history, each entry naming **what happened and where**. A run that changed nothing
93	logs nothing. (A repo that still carries a closed `Claudinite tracker: Conversation Extract` issue from when
94	the halves were two tasks keeps it as history — never post to it, never reopen it.)
95	
96	## Run on a capable model
97	
98	Deciding whether a lesson is genuinely new and durable — and deduping it against what's already documented —
99	is a **judgment call**, not mechanical extraction. A downgraded model adds noise or restates what's there,
100	and **auto-merge means no human reviews the PR before it lands** — CI gates correctness, not whether a
101	"lesson" earns its keep — so the capable-model requirement matters all the more. This task declares
102	`agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.
103	
104	## What this task must never do
105	
106	- **Never touch the shared canon** — this task writes only the repo's *own* local packs under
107	  `.claudinite/local/packs/`; everything else under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mount, and lifting a
108	  lesson up into the canon is the central promote task's job.
109	- **Never widen past the Context window** — the halves it declares live, the substantive commits and the
110	  touched PRs/issues named there are the scope; do not re-decide it. That includes the upgrade pass: this
111	  run's own additions, never the standing backlog.
112	- **Never merge `conversation-logs`** anywhere, and never rewrite its history — plain add and remove commits only.
113	- **Never paste the conversation onto an issue** — not raw JSONL, not a rendered transcript, not the turns
114	  themselves. Each landed rule gets one ≤200-word summary of the exchange behind it, and nothing more.
115	- **Never delete a log younger than retention, and never delete anything while `retention_days` is unset** —
116	  deletion is the ack that both passes happened.
117	- **Don't add noise** — a duplicate or hallucinated "lesson" is worse than adding nothing, the more so when
118	  its PR auto-merges with no human review to catch it.
119

1	---
2	name: extract-from-activity
3	description: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
4	---
5	
6	# Extract lessons from repo activity
7	
8	The **artifact** half of lesson extraction: mine what a window of work left behind — commits, the PRs
9	merged in it, the issue discussion around them — for durable, reusable lessons, and fold each into the
10	repo's **own local packs**. Its sibling [extract-from-conversations](../extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md)
11	mines the *dialogue*; this one never sees a conversation, only what the work committed.
12	
13	The **bar** a lesson must clear, the **local promotion ladder** it descends, and where a repo's capture
14	surface lives are shared with that sibling and stay canonical in
15	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — read it, don't re-derive it. What follows is only
16	what reading *artifacts* adds.
17	
18	## Capture at the repo's own level
19	
20	Write each lesson at whatever level reads naturally for this repo — refer to its files, services, or
21	mechanics wherever that's what makes the lesson clear. Don't force either extreme: don't contort a lesson
22	to be hyper-specific, and don't polish it into a general, portable rule. Making a lesson portable is the
23	growth lifecycle's **promote** stage, done canon-side later over whatever merged here; here, just capture
24	it usefully and let promotion lift whatever turns out to travel.
25	
26	## Read the window — and read merged PRs properly
27	
28	Work only the window you were handed (a scheduled run gets it as binding scope in the dispatch issue's
29	Context; an owner's ask names it in words). Never widen it.
30	
31	1. **The commits** — full bodies, and the diff wherever a fix is non-obvious.
32	2. **The PRs merged in the window** — read these *first* and read them *whole*: the diff **and** the
33	   review discussion. A merged PR is usually the window's richest lesson source, because it records what
34	   was tried, what a reviewer pushed back on, and why the landed shape won. A verdict reached in review
35	   is a lesson already argued; the commit alone shows only the winner.
36	3. **The issue activity** it names — the comments changed on those numbers.
37	
38	## What artifacts signal — and what they don't
39	
40	The signals worth converting here are the ones an artifact can carry: a fix whose diff is small but whose
41	*reason* is not obvious from the code; a review comment that names a convention the author missed; a
42	revert or a follow-up fix that says the first shape was wrong; a PR that grew several rounds because its
43	approach was re-decided mid-flight.
44	
45	**An already-settled, already-enforced implementation choice is not a lesson.** If a check or a test
46	already pins the shape — which roots a CI sweep walks, which contract a construction must satisfy — and
47	all that is left to say is *why it looks like that*, that explanation belongs as a comment at the
48	implementation site, not as prose in a pack. A rule earns its place by steering a **future** decision or
49	catching a **repeatable** mistake, not by narrating a past one that is already locked in.
50	
51	Wall-time and dialogue friction (a clarifying round-trip, a backtrack, a wait sat through) leave no trace
52	in a diff. Don't infer them from artifacts — that is the conversation sibling's territory, working from
53	logs that actually carry the timestamps.
54	
55	## Landing it
56	
57	Route each keeper down the ladder in [extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — check first,
58	then pack skill, prose last — into the local pack whose territory owns it. Write more checks and less
59	prose, and keep each addition terse and in the repo's own voice.
60	
61	A new check ships **green or not at all**: see it fail on a violating fixture and pass on a clean one. A
62	rule that cannot be made confident lands as prose instead — never as a broken check.
63	
64	Finding nothing is a perfectly good and common outcome; a duplicate or invented "lesson" is worse than
65	adding nothing.

1	---
2	name: extract-from-conversations
3	description: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
4	---
5	
6	# Extract lessons from a conversation
7	
8	The **dialogue** half of lesson extraction: read one agent ↔ user session — its turns *and* the actions
9	taken in it — and convert its friction into changes that make the **next** run faster, clearer, and less
10	dependent on human steering. Its sibling [extract-from-activity](../extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) mines
11	what the work committed; this one mines how the work went.
12	
13	The **bar** a lesson must clear, the **local promotion ladder** it descends, and where a repo's capture
14	surface lives stay canonical in [extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — read it, don't
15	re-derive it. What follows is only what reading a *conversation* adds.
16	
17	## The goal
18	
19	Every pass optimizes for one outcome: **the next run needs less.** Less clarification, less rework, less
20	waiting, less human steering. Read the session not as "what did we accomplish" but as "where did this
21	cost more than it should have, and what durable change removes that cost next time." If a pass can't name
22	a concrete next-time saving, it found nothing — and that's fine.
23	
24	## Where the conversation comes from
25	
26	- **A captured log** on the repo's orphan `conversation-logs` branch (`<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`),
27	  read with plain git in the checkout — `git show origin/conversation-logs:<file>`. The log carries
28	  per-entry timestamps, per-message token usage, and the `tool_use`/`tool_result` pairs behind every
29	  wall-time number, which is exactly what the measured analysis below needs. This is the routine path.
30	- **The live session**, when an owner asks in plain words for a retrospective. Same method; deliver the
31	  capture as a branch + PR **for a human to review**, never one that self-merges.
32	
33	**Never reflect-and-edit unprompted in the middle of a task** — it interrupts the work; the owner decides
34	when a session is done enough to mine.
35	
36	## What to look for — the friction signals
37	
38	Read the conversation end to end and hunt for these signatures. Each marks a place the loop cost more than
39	necessary, and each converts to a specific durable fix.
40	
41	### 1. Misunderstandings between agent and user
42	
43	The signs: a clarifying-question round-trip; the user correcting an assumption ("no, I meant…"); the agent
44	building the wrong thing and reworking it; the user restating the same request; an `AskUserQuestion` whose
45	answer was, in hindsight, the obvious default.
46	
47	**Convert to:** encode the resolved understanding so the next agent never has to ask. Every question the
48	user answered is a candidate **default**; every correction is a candidate **convention or glossary entry**;
49	a recurring wrong assumption is a candidate **confirm-first checkpoint placed earlier**, or a clearer doc
50	the agent reads cold and gets right the first time. The test of a good fix: next time the agent proceeds
51	correctly **without the round-trip**.
52	
53	### 2. Suboptimal agent actions
54	
55	The signs: the agent took an approach then backtracked; did redundant or repeated work; re-ran a command
56	that had already failed for a knowable reason; reached for a heavy tool where a light one fit; reinvented
57	something the codebase already provided; re-read a file it had just written to "verify"; missed an existing
58	convention and had it corrected in review.
59	
60	**Convert to:** a rule pointing at the right approach or tool, a pointer to the existing helper/convention
61	so it's found first, or a **footgun note placed where it'll be read** (the usage-site-vs-central call is in
62	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). The test: next time the agent takes the good path
63	first, not after a detour.
64	
65	### 3. Long wall-time waits — and measure them
66	
67	The signs: independent operations run **serially** that had no dependency and could have been parallel; a
68	padded fixed `sleep` that over- or under-shot; a process **waited out after its result was already in
69	hand**; blind long polling; re-running a check (e.g. CI) that was already green.
70	
71	**Measure, don't hand-wave.** Quantify the wait with real wall-clock numbers from the log's own timestamps
72	and separate the kinds of time — compute (a compile, a test/render run) vs. genuine **idle waiting**
73	(sleeps, polling, a finished process not yet killed). The numbers are computable, never estimated. A fix is
74	only credible against numbers; name the **single highest-leverage change** that shortens it, or conclude it
75	was already optimal.
76	
77	**Convert to:** a batch/parallelize rule, a poll-with-rolling-backoff instead of a blind sleep,
78	kill-the-process-once-its-output-is-in-hand, or merge-on-an-already-green-check. (These are the subject of
79	the standing **efficiency analysis** in [the unattended-agents skill](../unattended-agents/SKILL.md) — fold
80	a wall-time finding into that frame rather than re-deriving it.) The test: same result, less wall clock, no
81	loss of quality.
82	
83	## Encode the questions the user keeps asking
84	
85	The single highest-leverage move for **less human feedback**: the questions a user asks *repeatedly* are a
86	checklist the agent should run **itself.** If the user keeps asking "how many processes ran — could it be
87	fewer?", "what took longest?", "did you kill it the moment its work was done?", stop waiting to be asked —
88	fold those exact questions into a **standing self-check the agent answers proactively** at the end of the
89	relevant work, and close with a terse verdict (a concrete change, or an explicit "already optimal"). Each
90	recurring question converted this way is one the user never has to ask again — and it's where a *measured*
91	retrospective comes from: the user's recurring efficiency questions, answered pre-emptively, with numbers.
92	
93	## Two passes per log, and the second one may overturn the first
94	
95	A captured log gets a **fresh pass** within a day of capture and a **final hindsight pass** just before
96	retention deletes it, against the corpus as it stands by then. The hindsight pass is a real re-read, not a
97	formality: a friction signal that looked situational the first time may have recurred since, and a lesson
98	landed since may have made a keeper redundant. Both directions are legitimate outcomes.
99	
100	## Provenance: summarize the exchange, never paste it
101	
102	For each rule that actually **lands** from a log, post one short comment on the issue the log names
103	(`--issue-<n>--` in its filename; **`--issue-0--` means the capture had no associated issue**, so there is
104	nothing to post on and the rule simply lands without a comment):
105	
106	- one provenance line — the rule added, the capture date, the session id;
107	- then a **200-word-max** description of just the slice of conversation that caused the rule: what was
108	  asked, what went wrong or got corrected, and why the rule follows from it.
109	
110	**Summarize, never transcribe.** The dialogue itself is far too verbose for an issue — no pasted turns
111	beyond a short quoted phrase, never raw JSONL, never a rendered transcript. A log that yields nothing gets
112	**no** comment: extraction is the only path to permanence, and a log's conversation is gone once retention
113	deletes it. That is a deliberate call, so a padded "lesson" written to feel productive costs more than the
114	silence it replaced.
115

1	# Extracting lessons — the bar and the local promotion ladder
2	
3	> **Scope: what both extraction skills share.** This doc is the **bar** a lesson must clear and the
4	> **ladder** it descends once it clears it — the half that is identical whatever the lesson was mined
5	> from. What each *source* adds is owned by its own skill:
6	> [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) for commits, merged PRs and issue
7	> activity, and [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) for a session's
8	> dialogue. Both load this doc; neither restates it.
9	
10	Its callers are the growth pack's [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md) daily task, which runs
11	both skills over one window, and an owner's occasional plain-words ask for a retrospective.
12	
13	## Run the pass on a capable model
14	
15	Extraction is mechanical, but deciding *what clears the bar* is a judgment call a weaker model fails
16	silently — it ships a plausible-but-wrong "lesson" where a capable model correctly bails (see
17	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md), "Match the agent model to the judgment it
18	must make"). The terse rules that *govern* the pass — run it, plus the separate efficiency analysis — also
19	live there; this doc is the how-to.
20	
21	## From signal to lesson — the bar
22	
23	A signal is only worth writing down when the fix is **durable, reusable, and generalizable beyond this one
24	session or window.** Before adding anything:
25	
26	- **Dedupe ruthlessly** against the existing packs — a lesson already covered (even worded differently,
27	  even in another pack, even enforced by a check) is not a new lesson.
28	- **One-offs don't qualify.** A situational detail, a restatement of a generic truism, or something already
29	  implied by an existing rule is below the bar.
30	- **Promote what's portable.** A lesson true for projects beyond this one belongs in shared, cross-project
31	  canon, not stuck in one repo's local packs — the growth lifecycle's promote stage lifts it there
32	  centrally; capture it well locally and let promote generalize whatever travels.
33	
34	## Route to the local pack that owns it — the promotion ladder
35	
36	A project's capture surface is its **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/`); everything else
37	under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mounted canon and is never a capture target. Pick the pack whose
38	territory the lesson belongs to (most repos have one general pack; some segregate a domain pack), then
39	prefer the strongest mechanism it allows:
40	
41	1. **A check** in that pack's rules — author the `.mjs`, list it on the pack's `pack.mjs`, ship it with a
42	   red-first fixture. Its failure message *is* the lesson.
43	2. **A pack skill**, when the lesson is an activity-scoped procedure rather than a condition.
44	3. **Terse prose** in the pack's `RULES.md` — only what neither of the above can carry.
45	
46	Write **more checks and less prose**: a check relieves every session's context completely, where prose only
47	relocates it. When no pack's scope fits and the lesson warrants segregation, a new local pack is a
48	self-contained directory drop.
49	
50	**A gotcha tied to one call site is not a pack rule at all.** A trap from misusing a specific API, class, or
51	library goes as a **comment right at the usage site** — next to the call itself, where the next editor of
52	that line sees it — never collected into a centralized gotchas list. Co-locate it in a file's own header
53	comment when the trap spans the whole file and you'd only hit it *while editing that file*. Reserve a
54	central gotchas doc for what no single usage site owns: a trap you could hit *without* reading the relevant
55	file (a mistake of omission), or a cross-cutting invariant.
56	
57	## "No new lessons" is a valid — and common — result
58	
59	Most sessions and most windows yield nothing durable, and that's the expected outcome. Say so and write
60	nothing rather than padding the docs to look productive: a spurious or duplicative "lesson" pollutes the
61	canon and costs every future reader. **Default to no edit when unsure** — the bar is a genuinely new,
62	reusable insight, not a diary of what happened.
63

1	# grow_with_claudinite
2	
3	Opt into the **growth lifecycle** — declaring this pack enrolls a repo in contributing its hard-won
4	lessons up to the shared Claudinite canon, and in pruning its local packs once the canon owns them.
5	Seeded by default (`--init` + the one-time `grow-with-claudinite-seed` baseline migration for the
6	existing fleet), and **opt-out by removal**: baselining never re-adds it.
7	
8	This pack carries the **repo-side** stages of the growth lifecycle: capturing a repo's own
9	lessons into its local packs, and pruning them once the shared canon covers them. The central
10	**promote** stage — which lifts portable lessons up into the shared canon — is a home-only duty
11	that runs canon-side, not a repo-side task, so it lives outside this pack.
12	
13	Its scheduled work is four tasks under this pack's own `tasks/`, each discovered by the repo's
14	scheduler (`engine/scheduler/discover.mjs`) wherever the pack is declared:
15	
16	| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| `growth-extract` ([tasks/growth-extract/task.md](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) | the project changed in the window, or a log is past retention | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI, plus the prune on the logs branch |
19	| `growth-dedup` ([tasks/growth-dedup/task.md](tasks/growth-dedup/task.md)) | weekly, when the canon or the project's local packs moved in the week | a PR against the repo's `main` |
20	| `growth-discover-packs` ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) | weekly | a new **local** pack in the repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`, via a reviewed PR |
21	| `prose-to-checks-sweep` ([tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md](tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)) | weekly (no-ops cheaply on a quiet corpus) | a PR converting always-testable pack prose into checks |
22	
23	(Plus [usage-fold](tasks/usage-fold/task.md), the agentless daily fold described below.)
24	
25	## Extraction is one task over two sources
26	
27	`growth-extract` is the whole capture stage, and it runs **three skills** in order:
28	
29	1. [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) over the window's commits, merged
30	   PRs and issue discussion;
31	2. [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) over the logs captured
32	   from working sessions (plus the retention prune);
33	3. [prose-to-checks](skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) over the prose **that run just wrote**, to see
34	   whether any of it upgrades to a check before the PR opens.
35	
36	Everything lands in **one** auto-merging PR. The two extraction halves used to be two tasks firing in
37	the same nightly slot against the same local packs; they share the lesson bar, the promotion ladder
38	and the dedup surface ([extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md)), so the split bought nothing
39	and cost a second opus dispatch, a second PR, and two runs deduping against a corpus the other was
40	concurrently writing.
41	
42	The third step is why the standing `prose-to-checks-sweep` is **weekly**: fresh prose is already
43	offered a conversion the night it is written, so what the sweep sees is a backlog that moves on a
44	weekly clock.
45	
46	A member that wants the local stages without contributing lessons upstream **opts out of
47	promotion** on its own entry — `{ "id": "grow_with_claudinite", "config": { "promote": false } }`
48	— and the central promote stage skips it (absent or `true` = participate).
49	
50	## The conversation lifecycle — capture in-session, extract in the daily task, retention
51	
52	The pack also owns **extraction from working sessions**, replacing the old in-session post-merge
53	lessons pass. Capture and extraction split by what each needs: **capture** needs the live session
54	transcript, so it runs in-session (at merge, and again when the session ends); **extraction** only
55	reads the already-pushed logs, so it is the conversation half of the ordinary `growth-extract`
56	scheduled task — the logs branch is *in the repo*, so reading it, committing lessons to local packs,
57	and pruning are plain local git on the working tree; only posting the summary on the issue uses the
58	GitHub MCP tools.
59	
60	1. **Capture — a step in the merge-to-main skill** (in-session, where the transcript lives).
61	   Right after a merge lands:
62	   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
63	   (in the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`).
64	   Deterministic, seconds; it bundles the session transcript (sidechains inline, timestamp
65	   order), **scrubs enumeration-first** (every value the environment holds — `process.env`
66	   minus a short named allowlist of structural values, plus known credential stores — is
67	   redacted wherever it appears, with credential-shape patterns as the backstop; a secret the
68	   session itself transformed is beyond any static scrub, and push protection is the last
69	   net), and pushes one file per **capture event** onto the orphan **`conversation-logs`**
70	   branch: `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, commits marked `[skip ci]`.
71	   **Delta-aware, keyed on the session id:** every capture pushes only the entries after this
72	   session's previous capture, whatever event produced it, so any two events chain into
73	   disjoint files and a zero delta pushes nothing at all. Double-writing is therefore safe by
74	   construction, not by coordination — the property [`session-end.mjs`](session-end.mjs) relies
75	   on, so `pack.test.mjs` pins it directly.
76	   The branch is a **work queue, not an archive** — never merged; tips are cheap in shallow
77	   session clones and retention keeps them bounded.
78	1. **Capture — again, when the session ends** ([session-end.mjs](session-end.mjs), invoked by the
79	   engine's SessionEnd hook runner for every active pack that ships one). Same capture, with
80	   `--issue 0`: **`0` means "no associated issue"**, and the filename shape stays byte-identical
81	   on purpose — the retention prune, the `conversationLogs` signal and the extract's filename
82	   parse all already accept it, whereas a *new* shape would be invisible to the prune and become
83	   immortal on the branch. This event is what captures the sessions that never merge (a review, an
84	   investigation, a session that ended in a question) and the post-merge **tail** of the ones that
85	   do. **Best effort:** a container reclaimed by timeout never fires it, so nothing depends on it
86	   having run — every firing enriches the record, every miss leaves exactly the merge-only
87	   behaviour. An `issue-0` log has no issue for the extract to post its exchange
88	   summary on; nothing else about its lifecycle differs.
89	   **Unattended sessions capture through the same step, deliberately not through the hook.** A
90	   scheduled task's executor session ends by having its container reclaimed, which is exactly
91	   the ending no `SessionEnd` fires on — so the executor runs the engine's runner itself as its
92	   last step and names its dispatch issue in `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE`, which this step uses in
93	   place of `0`. Those logs therefore file under the task that ran (the dispatch issue's title
94	   names `pack/task`), and the work no human watched becomes as countable as the work one did.
95	2. **Fresh pass — the conversation half of [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)**
96	   (precondition: a substantive merge, or a log actually past retention so the age-based prune still
97	   runs on a quiet repo; local git on the repo's working tree, MCP only for the issue comment). It
98	   applies the [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) skill (the
99	   friction signals and the measured efficiency analysis, computable from the log's timestamps and
100	   token usage) over [extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md)'s shared bar, routes keepers into
101	   the member's local packs, and posts on the worked issue, for each rule that landed, a
102	   **200-word-max** summary of the slice of conversation that caused it — the dialogue itself is
103	   never pasted there, it is far too verbose for an issue —
104	   **extraction is the only path to permanence**: a log that yields no rule gets no comment,
105	   and its conversation is gone once retention deletes it (a deliberate owner call).
106	3. **Final pass and deletion** — once a log ages past `config.retention_days`, the same task
107	   re-reads it with ~a week of hindsight (the rethink window), then deletes it (the age-based
108	   precondition arm guarantees the prune runs even on a repo gone quiet). Every log gets exactly two
109	   judgment passes. **Unset retention = the prune deletes nothing** (capture-only, fail-safe).
110	
111	No adoption question over it — `retention_days` stays unset (hidden) by default, which is
112	fail-safe (capture-only). A project that wants the prune active sets `config.retention_days`
113	itself (10 is the recommended floor); nothing else to schedule, since extraction rides the
114	fleet's one daily run like the other growth tasks.
115	
116	## Skill-usage metrics — what the mounted skills actually do
117	
118	Mounting a skill only puts its name and one-line description into the session prompt; whether the
119	model ever **loads** it is discretion, and nothing recorded it. So the promotion ladder's
120	skill-vs-prose call had no empirical feedback: a skill whose trigger never fires looked exactly like
121	one that fires daily, and a "skill" that loads in every session (rules wearing a skill's clothes)
122	looked exactly like a genuinely activity-scoped one.
123	
124	The [usage-fold](tasks/usage-fold/task.md) task closes that loop — daily, agentless, seconds. It
125	counts skill loads **and their denominators** (captures, merges, sessions, user messages, user
126	commands) out of the logs this pack already captures, into
127	`.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`: day rows recomputed statelessly inside the raw retention
128	window, week rows appended once past a `foldedThrough` watermark. Denominators are the point — a raw
129	count cannot tell healthy-rare from broken, so the question is loads *against the sessions where that
130	skill's own declared trigger plausibly applied*. Zeros are implicit (a skill with no loads has no
131	key), which is what makes "never loads" visible: diff the file against the repo's mounted skills.
132	
133	Fleet-wide aggregation is deliberately **not** here — the canon knows mechanisms, never repos. It is
134	the sheepdog pack's [`fleet-usage`](../sheepdog/tasks/fleet-usage/task.md) task, in the fleet-enforcer
135	repo, which is the only place that knows who the members are.
136	
137	## Rules
138	
139	| Rule | Kind | What |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| `growth-config` | hardcoded ([config-check.mjs](config-check.mjs)) | entry config shape valid |
142	
143	**Pack discovery** ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) is
144	an ordinary weekly task on the repo's own scheduler. The repo runs the whole pipeline over
145	**itself**: manifest its stack, hold it against the canon packs already on its shelf and its own
146	existing local packs, and — for genuinely project-specific knowledge neither homes — author a new
147	**local** pack populated from its real usage, landed through a **reviewed** PR (a new pack ships new
148	`.mjs` checks, and a check can break CI — the same reason `prose-to-checks-sweep` is reviewed, and
149	the one place this stage differs from extract). It writes only the repo's own
150	`.claudinite/local/packs/`; lifting a local pack up into the shared canon is the central promote
151	task's job.
152	
153	## Identifying a project's capture surface: its local packs (the same way in every stage)
154	
155	Every growth stage operates on a project's **local packs** — the tracked packs a repo keeps under
156	`.claudinite/local_packs/<pack>/` (prose in `RULES.md`, checks in the pack's `rules`, activity
157	procedures as the pack's skills, scheduled tasks under its `tasks/`). That subtree **is** the
158	project's own content;
159	the rest of `.claudinite/` is the **read-only mounted canon** and is never a capture, prune, or
160	promote target. So "a project's local packs" means precisely *everything under
161	`.claudinite/local_packs/`, and nothing else under `.claudinite/`*. This is the normalized capture
162	surface — a structural set the stages read the same way, not a `CLAUDE.md`-graph walk over stray
163	Markdown (a repo with no local packs yet simply has nothing to extract, dedup, or promote here; a
164	project adopts the structure via the `generate-project-instructions` skill).
165	
166	Prefer the strongest mechanism the lesson allows — the **local promotion ladder**, applied at the
167	project's own level: a deterministic rule becomes a **check** in the owning pack's `rules` (its
168	failure message carries the lesson), an activity-scoped procedure becomes a **pack skill**, and only
169	what neither can carry lands as **prose** in a pack's `RULES.md`. A check relieves every session's
170	context completely where prose only relocates it, so capture writes *more checks and less prose*.
171	
172	The stages differ only in *how they read that set*, never in *which set it is*: extract and dedup
173	run against the member repo and read the local packs from the working tree; promote runs centrally
174	and reads the same subtree over the GitHub API (get-file-contents under `.claudinite/local_packs/`).
175	Extract writes into it, promote reads from it, dedup prunes within it — all against the identical,
176	`.claudinite/local_packs/`-rooted set.
177

content.content:
1	---
2	name: prose-to-checks
3	description: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
4	---
5	
6	# Convert existing prose to checks
7	
8	A completeness-critic over a repo's own packs: prose that is always-testable but was never converted
9	becomes a check, so the packs keep shedding context over time instead of only at the moment a rule is
10	first learned.
11	
12	## Two callers, differing only in scope
13	
14	- **The upgrade pass**, as the last step of a
15	  [growth-extract](../../tasks/growth-extract/task.md) run: the scope is the prose **that run just
16	  wrote**. Extraction already descends the promotion ladder per lesson, but a lesson written as prose
17	  under time pressure is exactly where a convertible rule hides, so it gets asked once more before the
18	  PR opens. Never widen from here into the standing backlog.
19	- **The weekly [prose-to-checks-sweep](../../tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)**: the scope is the
20	  **standing backlog** — everything under the pack paths configured for this repo, which the task
21	  passes in its Context. A consuming repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/`) by
22	  default — projects don't improve core canon packs — while **Claudinite itself** also sweeps its core
23	  `packs/`. Read the prose under those paths (each pack's `RULES.md`, and any `SKILL.md` beside them).
24	
25	Plus on demand, when someone asks. Either way: never edit a read-only mounted canon pack under
26	`.claudinite/shared/`. Everything below is identical for both callers.
27	
28	## First gate — a working rule, not a product statement
29	
30	Before asking whether a rule is *testable*, ask whether it belongs to a pack at all: **does it govern
31	how we work, or state what the product does?** A pack — canon or local — homes the conventions,
32	gotchas and review discipline that recur across tasks whatever the feature happens to be. A rule
33	asserting which entities exist, what a surface must render, or that a feature's parts are wired to
34	each other is a **requirement**; its home is the project's executable spec and the suite that proves
35	it (the full rule lives in
36	[generate-project-instructions](../generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md)).
37	
38	This gate comes **first** because product statements sail through the check-the-world test below —
39	"this module must export `X`" has an obvious static signature. Converting one splits a feature's
40	definition across two systems and lands half of it in the one no test of the product ever reads.
41	Load-bearingness is not the test: a real gap in product coverage is a *requirements* gap.
42	
43	A product statement already sitting in pack prose is mis-homed, and a sweep is not the place to
44	re-home it. **Leave the prose and log it** as a mis-homed rule, the same way an un-checkable
45	candidate is logged — never cement it as a check.
46	
47	## What to look for — the check-the-world test
48	
49	For each rule that cleared the gate, ask the one question from
50	[engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md): **does it constrain a *static
51	signature in the repo artifact* — something a post-hoc scan could observe?**
52	
53	- **Yes → a conversion candidate.** A dangling-reference rule, a filename convention, a workflow
54	  or manifest shape, a "these two files must agree" invariant, a forbidden pattern in code.
55	- **No → leave it.** In-flight process (leaves no artifact — "see the test fail first"),
56	  judgment ("name by scope"), or knowledge whose failure is only visible at runtime (jsdom
57	  diverging from Chrome). These are why the rule is prose; don't force them.
58	
59	**A static signature is necessary, not sufficient.** Both shapes the working-discipline rules bar
60	— a rule that pins today's code in place, and one derivable from the product's requirements —
61	answer *yes* here, so screen every candidate against that bar before converting it. Leave either
62	where it is; routing a requirement to the spec and its suite is its own change, not this sweep's.
63	
64	The check-the-world rule from DESIGN holds: if a rule is always-testable, it was never really
65	part of the on-demand skill — it belongs in a pack as a check.
66	
67	## How to convert one
68	
69	Follow the extract stage's check-authoring discipline (the local promotion ladder in
70	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). For each candidate:
71	
72	> **The upgrade-pass caller lands inside growth-extract's own PR**, which auto-merges after CI — so the
73	> see-it-fail fixture is the only gate a converted check gets there. Convert only what you can prove;
74	> anything shakier stays prose and waits for the weekly sweep's reviewed PR.
75	
76	1. **Author the check** in the owning pack (`<pack>/<rule>.mjs`, listed in its `pack.mjs`) — the
77	   failure message *is* the rule (what / why / fix / `doc:` pointer back to the prose).
78	2. **Write the fixture first and see it fail** — a violating fixture must find, a clean one must
79	   not (the test lives beside the pack's other tests). A conversion with no proving fixture
80	   doesn't ship.
81	3. **Ship at real severity, fail-fast** — blocking for a defect, advisory only when the rule is
82	   directional by kind.
83	4. **Delete the prose the check now covers** — whole, never trimmed. The deletion test below is
84	   how you decide which paragraphs those are.
85	
86	**Before writing a rule off as un-checkable, try parsing the file's structure instead of grepping
87	its text.** Grep finds the pattern anywhere; parsing finds it in the one spot the rule means —
88	which kills the false alarm. (Example: `Authorization` is only wrong inside a CloudFront policy's
89	*own* header list, not elsewhere in the template.) Parse only as much as you need, and hold the
90	check to the same fixture bar.
91	
92	When even a scoped parser can't make detection confident, **leave the prose and log the
93	candidate** to a tagged conversion-backlog issue rather than shipping a shaky check.
94	
95	## Coming out: the deletion test
96	
97	Coming out of a conversion, apply the **deletion test**: prose a mechanism fully covers is
98	deleted, never trimmed. Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — *with this
99	paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent
100	how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete it whole. The check's failure message is where
101	the rule lives now and its header comment is where the rationale lives, so a paragraph restating
102	either pays twice and is the drift trap waiting to spring.
103	
104	Before concluding prose is the only carrier, look at the pack's **skills** too — an
105	activity-scoped skill often already holds the map a rule is repeating. Keep only what no artifact
106	carries.
107	
108	The test **discriminates** rather than just deleting: a paragraph stays whole whenever it carries
109	something the check does not — a second rule in the same breath, an exemption the check can't
110	encode, a value the check can't judge, or a remedy the finding's own `fix` line never states
111	(a finding renders `what` / `why` / `fix` / `doc`, never the rule's `description`, so a remedy
112	that lives only in the description is not carried). Two worked calls: an `npm test` invariant
113	went entirely — the check caught it and the testing-guide skill already listed the suites —
114	while an `extension-test/` mirror bullet stayed, because the check beside it enforced only the
115	`package.json` list's sync with the tree and never the mirror convention itself.
116	
117	Whether a check covers a rule is a judgment about meaning, so this test is applied by a
118	**reader**, not mechanized.
119	
120	## Bounds
121	
122	- **One PR, bounded surface** — the new rule module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixture, and the
123	  trimmed prose. Don't "improve" unrelated rules while you're in there.
124	- **Never delete a rule you didn't convert** — the deletion test is only ever asked of a rule a
125	  *landed* check now enforces.
126	- Run the suite and the sweep green before the PR goes up, and never push to `main` directly. The
127	  sweep opens its own PR for the owner's approval; the upgrade pass adds its conversion to the
128	  growth-extract PR already being opened, and opens none of its own.
129

content.content:
1	# Claudinite — the canon's own non-portable working rules
2	
3	This is the Claudinite home repo's own local pack: the capture surface for lessons that are
4	**specific to working on the canon itself** and would not make sense mounted into a consuming
5	project. Portable lessons — anything true for repos beyond this one — belong in the shared canon
6	under `packs/`/`skills/` instead (proposed by PR, or lifted by the promote stage).
7	
8	The growth lifecycle writes here automatically: the `growth-extract` daily task routes the canon's
9	own non-portable lessons — mined from repo activity and from captured conversations alike — into
10	this pack (each at the local promotion ladder's strongest mechanism — a check where the rule is deterministic, otherwise terse
11	prose below).
12	
13	## Standing owner decisions — settled, do not re-litigate
14	
15	- **`canon-curation` lives in `.claudinite/local/packs/`, not `packs/`** (owner decision,
16	  2026-07-19). The canon home's curation duties are Claudinite-maintaining-Claudinite —
17	  project-specific content on the home's own capture surface. Do not propose moving it back, and
18	  do not describe the move as open or provisional.
19	- **Local-pack `run_daily` scheduling is ON — the fleet's default path** (same decision). The
20	  planner reads every member's local-pack daily descriptors by default; never reintroduce an
21	  "experimental / not enabled" framing or an opt-in seam for it.
22	- **Packs-tree segregation is barriers configuration only.** Any rule about what the `packs/`
23	  tree may reference is expressed by declaring/configuring the `barriers` pack (contributed
24	  edges, `siblings`/`scope` capabilities — extend barriers generically if a capability is
25	  missing). Never write standalone code that checks packs-tree segregation.
26	- **A `docs/<initiative>/DESIGN.md` records the mechanism only** (owner decision, 2026-07-23,
27	  #420). Status, phase tracking, in-flight-PR reconciliation and remaining work live in that
28	  initiative's tracking issue (agent-preprocessing → #394); a phased plan lives in the sibling
29	  `MIGRATION.md`. Don't reintroduce a status / open-questions / remaining-work section there.
30	- **Multi-session work hands off through the tracking issue, never a prepared prompt** (owner
31	  correction, 2026-07-23). The owner's opener is `continue work on #<n>`, so state not written
32	  into the issue is lost. Before ending a session on unfinished work, update the issue and let
33	  the session summary be a pointer to it — never compose a bespoke "pick up from here" prompt.
34	- **The canon never knows which repos consume it — fleet-wide aggregation is Sheepdog's domain**
35	  (owner correction, 2026-07-28, #520). Designing anything that spans repos, the tempting shape is
36	  a member list (or a "fleet" task) living in the canon. It doesn't go here: the canon carries only
37	  **mechanisms exercised on itself**, and the knowledge of *which* repos exist stays in the
38	  **Sheepdog** repo and its pack, which enumerates members at runtime from its own
39	  `.claudinite-checks.json` entry — exactly where `fleet-census` and `fleet-freshness` already keep
40	  it. So a cross-repo feature splits in two: a self-contained per-repo half in the canon, and the
41	  aggregation half as a Sheepdog fleet task. **No repo list exists anywhere in canon code** — and a
42	  derived fleet artifact lands in Sheepdog as a daily **auto-merged PR of a `GENERATED` file**,
43	  never a direct commit to its `main`.
44	- **A pack default stays in the pack — don't ask it at adoption, don't write it into a member's
45	  config** (owner ruling, 2026-07-28, #527/#528). An adoption question whose recommended answer is
46	  right for nearly everyone is "bad noise": it taxes every adopting repo to re-state the default,
47	  and materializing that answer into `.claudinite-checks.json` freezes a copy that then drifts from
48	  the pack and has to be migrated. Keep the default in the pack's own code, ask nothing, and let the
49	  rare project that wants to differ add the setting by hand. Read config as *optional* — an unset
50	  key means "the default", never "misconfigured" (`retention_days` unset is precisely why the
51	  growth-extract retention prune is skipped rather than failing).
52	
53	## Canon-specific gotchas
54	
55	- **Baselining backfill skips the home.** The nightly baselining that lands a `seededByDefault`
56	  pack (and canon-delivered declaration changes) on every member is gated `!isHome`, so the canon
57	  home is the one repo it never reaches: what the fleet receives automatically, this repo's own
58	  `.claudinite-checks.json` only ever gets by hand.
59	- **Pack discovery imports the whole pack tree eagerly — declaration is irrelevant.**
60	  `discoverPacks` imports every `packs/<name>/pack.mjs` on disk and `scanSkillChecks` imports
61	  every `<pack>/skills/<skill>/checks.mjs` beside it, *before* activation is consulted. So
62	  anything in that import graph loads in every repo under every declaration, and a module that is
63	  also a CLI entry point gets re-imported while it is still evaluating: a top-level `await` in its
64	  entry block then never settles and Node exits 13 having run nothing (#581 — `interview.mjs
65	  check` deadlocked fleet-wide, invisible because the SessionStart orchestrator's fail-soft reads
66	  it as a merely-absent note). Start the work *after* evaluation completes — `check(…).catch(…)`.
67	  Enforced by `pack-discovery-entry-await`; the corollary it can't check is to keep these modules
68	  import-light in the first place.
69	- **Green canon CI is not evidence about a consumer — the canon's own packs are always already
70	  migrated.** The one thing canon CI cannot exercise is what a canon change does to a repo on its
71	  *next* baselining, and every consumer-breaking change so far passed it cleanly: #555 (manifest
72	  became a closed vocabulary → 11 local packs across 10 repos silently stopped running their
73	  checks), #585 (PR-open status never read → 12 repos frozen two days while the run reported
74	  `ok`), #588 (auto-merge armed where no PR CI exists → a PR that never lands). All were invisible
75	  until a consumer ran. So when a change adds or requires a manifest field, moves a check's
76	  severity or id, or alters a vendored contract, say in the PR *which* consumer-side evidence
77	  carries it — a migration record, or a demonstration that an unmigrated member stays green — and
78	  never treat a green canon suite as that evidence (#592 tracks the missing gate).
79	- **A pack's `RULES.md` is injected into every session that declares the pack — an idea nobody can
80	  act on belongs in `docs/`, and a pack file must not link there.** Deferred directions, blocked
81	  proposals and status live in `docs/` (e.g. `docs/future-directions.md`) precisely because pack
82	  prose costs context in every consumer session. And the pointer cannot go the other way: `docs/`
83	  is outside the vendor set, so a link from any file under `packs/` resolves to nothing in every
84	  consumer — the `reference-integrity` class that reached `main` unnoticed in #424 (and that
85	  check is work-scoped, so it only sees paths the branch itself deletes). Reference `docs/` from
86	  the issue or PR instead.
87	- **Pick a scheduled task's cadence from how often its signal actually moves.** On a member the
88	  mounted canon changes most nights — baselining converges `.claudinite/shared/` daily — so any
89	  precondition reading `sharedMount` fires nearly every night, spending an opus dispatch per
90	  firing. Where the work isn't latency-sensitive (pruning, dedup), a stale item stays harmlessly
91	  correct, so daily buys noise, not freshness: `growth-dedup` moved to `weekly` in #583 and loses
92	  nothing, because the signals are window-scoped (`sinceIso`) and `windowStart` widens to the
93	  widest due task's period — a weekly run sees all 7 days, batched rather than dropped.
94	- **The home doesn't declare `git-github`, so its skills never mount — never conclude "no such
95	  skill" from `.claude/skills/`.** `mount-skills.mjs` filters on the *literal* declaration
96	  (`isActive(p, { packs: declared })`), not the `requires` closure `check_the_world.mjs` resolves,
97	  and the baselining that would normalize that closure into `.claudinite-checks.json` is the one
98	  thing gated `!isHome` — so `merge-to-main` and `git-github-advanced` are simply absent here.
99	  Read `packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` out of the tracked tree — the corpus *is* this repo,
100	  and an unmounted skill says nothing about whether its procedure applies. The seeding gap above
101	  is a different one (`git-github` arrives by closure, never `seededByDefault`); catching this
102	  one needs `resolveDeclaredPacks` compared against the literal declaration.
103	- **Never re-serialize a repo's JSON config to apply an edit — patch the text.** A round-trip
104	  rewrites what it wasn't asked to: Python's `json.dump` defaults to `ensure_ascii=True` (every
105	  non-ASCII character becomes a `\uXXXX` escape), and indent, key order and the trailing newline
106	  become the serializer's opinion. Nothing fails and tests stay green, so it rides onward. Edit
107	  JSON as anchored text; if you must round-trip, pin every lossy default and read the resulting
108	  diff before committing. (Portable — a promote candidate for `repo-text-sweeps`, where a
109	  `\uXXXX`-in-tracked-JSON check would carry it.)
110	- **Test git fixtures must commit with signing off.** `engine-tests/helpers.mjs`'s `makeRepo`
111	  overrides identity but not signing, so all 31 call sites route fixture commits through the
112	  signing service; when it degrades, each commit blocks on it and the suite leaks descriptors
113	  (~800 per full run against a 4096 cap) until `git commit` and `git push` fail process-wide.
114	  Commit with `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit --no-gpg-sign`: signing a tmpdir throwaway
115	  buys nothing. (Portable — a promote candidate for `writing-tests`.)
116	- **A canon session with a consumer repo also in its sources will reach for the *consumer's*
117	  merge skill — merge by the skill of the repo you are merging into.** Canon work is routinely
118	  dual-repo (the canon plus the fleet member being piloted), and both repos ship a merge skill
119	  under different names — the canon's `packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/` and, say, GCEC's
120	  local `merge-and-ci`. The consumer's skill wins the match on name/description and is followed
121	  to the letter, so the canon-only steps in *its* recipe are silently skipped — repeatedly, the
122	  **post-merge conversation capture** (`node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue
123	  <n>`, the "After the merge" section of `merge-to-main`). So: before merging in a dual-repo
124	  session, resolve the merge skill **by target repo**, not by which skill matched first — and
125	  treat capture as part of the merge, not as an optional epilogue.
126	- **Fail-soft SessionStart steps hide their own breakage fleet-wide — test the emitted
127	  output, not the exit code.** Every `engine/pack_loader/` SessionStart step
128	  (`inject-pack-prose.mjs`, `mount-skills.mjs`, `env-requirements.mjs`) wraps its body in
129	  `try { ... } catch {}` so a broken loader never blocks a session. That fail-soft is deliberate,
130	  but it means a runtime fault — a wrong dynamic-import target, a renamed module — exits 0 and
131	  simply emits nothing: no error, no signal. And because the engine is vendored verbatim into
132	  every member, one canon regression silently disables that step across the whole fleet at once.
133	  So a step like this must be guarded by a regression test that runs the real script against a
134	  real corpus and asserts the **positive** effect — prose IS emitted — never merely that
135	  `status === 0` (which fail-soft makes meaningless); see
136	  `engine-tests/pack_loader/inject-pack-prose.test.mjs`.
137	- **The nightly self-refresh cannot repair the vendor-set computation — pin operational
138	  files against the REAL canon tree.** Baselining's converge re-runs
139	  `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs` from canon HEAD, so a bug *in that computation* is
140	  the one class of canon regression that is not self-healing: every refresh faithfully
141	  reproduces it, and recovery is an out-of-band vendor refresh applied to each member by
142	  hand. So when the vendor set excludes by *pattern*, an operational file that matches
143	  needs a by-path whitelist (`VENDORED_ENGINE_DOCS`) **and** a regression test asserting
144	  against the real canon tree, not only a synthetic fixture: a fixture keeps proving the
145	  whitelist mechanism works while the live path silently drops out from under it (see the
146	  paired tests in `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.test.mjs`).
147	- **A check that selects its inputs by path pattern can reach zero files and still pass — assert
148	  the live in-scope count.** When skills moved inside their owning pack (#385),
149	  `skill-no-enforcement-narration` kept scanning the root-level `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` layout: it
150	  matched nothing in any tree, read as live, and caught nothing until a human noticed the prose it
151	  should have flagged (#560 — 21 skills in scope once repointed). Its fixtures are why it hid so
152	  well; they spelled the same dead layout, so five green tests proved the *matching* and never the
153	  *selection*. A scan-based check therefore needs one assertion over the **real** tree that its
154	  scope is non-empty. Other half of the same class: agent-facing text pointing where the code isn't
155	  — the same PR fixed a rule whose `why`, fix text and `doc` all named `engine/checks_helpers` or
156	  `checks/lib`, neither of which ever existed. Nothing catches that on its own —
157	  `reference-integrity` is work-scoped and flags only paths the branch itself deletes — so grep the
158	  tree for any directory you name in a finding, a remedy, or a doc pointer before shipping it.
159	- **A scheduled task's precondition gates on movement in the window, never on standing state.** "An
160	  open PR exists" is true forever once it is true once, so the task wakes every night, spends an
161	  agent, and re-derives yesterday's verdict over an unchanged set (three of tidy-repo's tasks
162	  shipped that way; fixed in #554). Gate on the objects' own movement — a `touched` list or a
163	  tip-commit date, which the signal collector has to actually carry (`branches` carried names only,
164	  so "is any of this new" had no answer at all). A signal that is true most days on an active repo
165	  — a substantive `main` move — may only **widen** an already-triggered run, never wake one. And the
166	  gate is not the scope: where a verdict is relative to the rest of the set (superseded-by,
167	  already-in-`main`), newness gates and the full set stays the scope. (Portable — a promote
168	  candidate for `basics/scheduled-tasks.md`, which states the precondition contract but not this.)
169	- **You cannot force a due slot by running the scheduler workflow by hand.** Dueness is
170	  stateless — a slot is due iff its time falls in `(last successful run, now]` — so a
171	  `workflow_dispatch` run outside the slot's window succeeds, prints `- no tasks due`, and
172	  does nothing. It looks like a healthy run. To exercise a task Action-side, invoke its
173	  worker directly, or move the slot hour in `taskScheduler` and wait for the cron.
174	- **A scheduled task is gated twice — prove a change through `planRun`, never through its own
175	  precondition.** `planRun` computes the due list *before* any precondition runs, so a task whose
176	  most-recent slot has already been run is never evaluated and never reads its signals at all. #513's
177	  forced-run override landed with every test driving the precondition (or the signal collector) directly
178	  and was inert on exactly the run it existed for — the mid-day manual trigger — because the due-list
179	  gate it never touched had already dropped the task (`evaluations: []`; fixed in #516). A test that
180	  starts *inside* the gate proves only "works once evaluated" and says nothing about whether the task
181	  ever gets there. Drive the real `planRun` from a deliberately **non-due** slot: that is the only shape
182	  that catches it.
183	- **Every due task in a run shares ONE checkout — an agentless worker must not touch it.** The
184	  scheduler runs the whole due list in a single working tree, so a worker that checks out a branch or
185	  leaves an index behind hands the next task a tree it did not expect, and a run that dies leaves the
186	  mess for whatever follows. A task whose output is a regenerated file lands it through
187	  `engine/scheduler/deliver-generated.mjs` — git plumbing against the fetched base tip, with HEAD, the
188	  index and the working tree untouched — and reads its prior state from that base rather than local
189	  HEAD, so stacked runs stay idempotent. (`basics/baselining`'s own deliver is the deliberate
190	  exception: it commits a whole working tree under the member's delivery preference.)
191	- **A code-search hit is evidence; a code-search miss is not — survey by reading each file.**
192	- **Derive the test file list from the tree — every hand-written glob here under-runs the suite.**
193	  There is no `package.json` and no test script, so each session invents its own incantation and
194	  silently verifies less than it thinks. Measured in this checkout: `node --test <dir>` does not
195	  recurse — it resolves the path as a module and dies with `Cannot find module`; bash `**` is not
196	  recursive without `globstar`, so `engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs` reaches
197	  **37 of 65** tracked test files. Four consecutive sessions (2026-07-26, #459/#452/#435/#468) each
198	  wrote a different command and reported 587, 690, 621 and 697 tests — three of them pushed after
199	  running a strict subset. Neither published list is authoritative either: `ci.yml`'s `tests=(…)`
200	  array omits `vendoring/*.test.mjs`, and `engine/checks/README.md`'s "as CI runs it" one-liner
201	  names `engine/test/`, `skills/` and `mount/`, none of which exist. So enumerate from git and let
202	  the count speak: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`. (The drift-guard, once the array is
203	  clean: assert every tracked `*.test.mjs` is matched by `ci.yml`'s globs.)
204	- **A branch that waited overnight has lost its base *and* possibly its premise — re-verify the
205	  problem still exists on current `main`, unasked.** This repo merges its own scheduled-task PRs
206	  without a human, on top of multi-phase migrations that retire whole directories: measured on
207	  PR #465, `main` moved **14 commits in 13.7 hours** and one of them (#473, "retire `run_daily/`")
208	  *deleted the file the PR's diagnosis rested on* and had already landed most of its content. The
209	  branch rebased cleanly and the tests stayed green — the change was simply no longer the change to
210	  make, and the correct move was `git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` and re-applying only the
211	  surviving slice (9 files → 2). So syncing the base is not the check; the check is a **content**
212	  one: after `git fetch`, read what the new commits did to the surface you are changing and state
213	  whether the problem is still there, what the goal was, and what survives. Do this whenever you
214	  return to a paused branch, before presenting it — the owner should never have to ask "is this
215	  change still needed" (asked three times on #465 before it was volunteered).
216	- **Every `Claude_Code_Remote` call costs minutes, and a call that returns nothing has NOT failed —
217	  never re-issue it.** The whole server behaves this way, not one tool: measured over four sessions
218	  on 2026-07-29, `add_repo` ran 270–285s a call, `send_later` 117–390s, `list_triggers` 139–325s,
219	  `delete_trigger` 286–301s, `subscribe_pr_activity` 14–237s. They read like cheap registrations,
220	  so a session issues one, sits through minutes of silence, concludes it hung, and issues it again —
221	  and *the duplicate is the dominant cost*, because the first call had already succeeded:
222	  **#562 (`2026-07-29T1500Z`) — 6 `add_repo` calls, 1121s of that session's 1391s of tool
223	  wall-clock (81%)**, with `HelloWorldFlutterApp` added twice (285s + 271s); **#553
224	  (`2026-07-29T2206Z`) — the same PR check-in `send_later`d 4 times, 1107s of 2028s (55%)**; **#544
225	  (`2026-07-29T1248Z`) — `list_triggers` ×2, `delete_trigger` ×2 on one trigger id, `send_later` ×2:
226	  1854s of 2472s (75%)**, in a session whose real work was 166 tool calls. `AskUserQuestion` shares
227	  the shape — #559's session asked one question twice for 218s + 204s. So: **one call per intent,
228	  ever**, and when what you want is "is it green yet", read the check status directly and merge on
229	  the already-green result rather than buying a notification. Budget these calls before making them:
230	  four of them is most of an hour.
231	- **Sync local `main` with `git reset --hard origin/main`, never `git pull` — this repo's session
232	  clones are shallow.** The post-merge sync step of `merge-to-main` is where it bites, and it bit
233	  five separate sessions on 2026-07-29 alone (#548, #551, #537, #559 and the session-end capture of
234	  `73a4db48`). A shallow clone has no common ancestor with the fetched remote, so `git pull` either
235	  demands an explicit strategy or reports the stale local ref as carrying unique commits it does not
236	  have — and the tempting reading, "local `main` has work the remote lacks", is wrong every time:
237	  the session's own work is already *in* `origin/main`, which is why it just merged. #537's session
238	  spent 87s across `git pull`, `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` and log comparisons proving
239	  that from scratch; #559's landed on "git sees no common ancestor" the same way. Nothing of value
240	  is ever on this repo's local `main`, so the sync is unconditional: `git fetch origin main && git
241	  reset --hard origin/main`. (Portable — a promote candidate for `git-github`'s merge procedure,
242	  where "your clone may be shallow" is true of any container-hosted session.)
243	- **The home has no `.claudinite/shared/` mount — machinery paths must accept both roots.** A
244	  consumer runs the vendored engine under `.claudinite/shared/engine/…` with packs under
245	  `.claudinite/(shared|local)/packs/…`; the home *is* the corpus and runs the same code from the
246	  repo root. So a path, regex, or workflow command written to the consumer mount shape works
247	  fleet-wide and fails on exactly this repo — the last place anyone exercises it, so the break
248	  surfaces late. Write the two-root form up front: make the `.claudinite/(shared|local)/` prefix
249	  optional in a pattern, and in a command probe for `.claudinite/shared/` first, falling back to
250	  the repo root.
251	- **Tightening a contract that member-owned files must satisfy has NO carrier — baseline
252	  migrations move paths, not schemas — so it lands as a fleet-wide silent break.** Vendoring
253	  refreshes `.claudinite/shared/` only; a member's `.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/pack.mjs` is
254	  the member's own content, which no converge may edit. And `migrations/` cannot help: its record
255	  is a path relocation (`aliases: [{ canonical, legacy }]`, applied by `applyFileAliases`), so it
256	  has no way to express "the field `rules` is now `worldRules`/`workRules`" or "`ruleRoutingGuidance`
257	  is now required" — exactly what #555 tightened, shipping no record because there was none to
258	  ship. The break is worse than loud: `normalizeManifest` returns `{ ...mod, rules }` with `rules`
259	  rebuilt **only** from the two scoped keys, so a legacy manifest's array is overwritten with `[]`

262	  hand in one session, and the members' own pack tests asserted `pack.rules` and went red on CI
263	  the moment the manifests moved. So before tightening anything a member's own file must satisfy,
264	  ask what carries it across the fleet; if the answer is "nothing", the change is not ready —
265	  accept the legacy shape in `normalizeManifest` (and say so) until a carrier exists, and never
266	  let a stale declaration degrade to *fewer checks running* rather than a failure.

268	  the artifact — check the response, and alarm on the stamp.** `deliver()` in

270	  never read `status`, so a 403 (the member's *"Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull
